question: What do the different columns in the stock moves history report show, like the reference and status fields?
reference: The Moves History report columns include Date (calendar date and time of the move), Reference (reason for the move, such as a receipt number like WH/IN/00012), Product, Lot/Serial Number, From and To locations, Quantity, Unit of measure, and Status (such as Done).

question: How can I make Odoo pick the smallest number of packages when fulfilling an order for a product?
reference: Enable the Packages feature, then set the product category's Force Removal Strategy to Least Packages. With this strategy, Odoo uses the fewest packages to fulfill an order, so for example an order of 80 kg of flour stored in 100 kg packages will pull from an unopened 100 kg package rather than the partially used 54 kg one.

question: What do the international trade terms like EXW or CIF mean, and which ones are available in Odoo?
reference: Incoterms are standardized trade terms that define the rights and responsibilities of buyers and sellers regarding delivery, risk transfer, and cost distribution. By default, all 11 Incoterms are available in Odoo: EXW, FCA, FAS, FOB, CFR, CIF, CPT, CIP, DPU, DAP, and DDP.

question: How do I set the Intrastat region for my company, and what if I have warehouses in different regions?
reference: For Belgian companies, go to Accounting > Configuration > Settings, select the Company Intrastat Region where the company is located, and Save. If your warehouses are in more than one region, set the Intrastat region per warehouse instead via Inventory > Configuration > Warehouses, selecting a warehouse, setting its region, and saving.

question: How do I purchase more credits for digitizing documents in Odoo?
reference: Go to the Settings app (or Accounting > Configuration > Settings), find the Digitization section, and click Buy credits. Note that XML files don't consume credits since they're processed without OCR.

question: When does Odoo automatically recalculate taxes on a quote or invoice?
reference: Taxes are recalculated automatically at several trigger points, including when the sales rep sends the quote by email, when the customer views the online quote or invoice on the portal, when a quote is confirmed into a sales order, when a draft invoice is validated, when a subscription generates an invoice, and when the customer reaches the last screen of the eCommerce checkout.

question: How do I see the purchase order that was automatically created for a dropshipped product on a sales order, and how do I confirm the delivery once the customer receives it?
reference: Open the sales order in the Sales app under Orders > Orders and click the Purchase smart button to view the associated RFQ; once confirmed it becomes a purchase order with a linked dropship receipt, viewable via the Dropship smart button. When the product is delivered to the customer, click Validate at the top-left of the dropship receipt to confirm the delivered quantity.

question: How does Odoo prove that my posted accounting entries haven't been tampered with?
reference: Odoo generates a unique SHA-256 hash (fingerprint) for each secured entry based on its essential fields, and chains each entry's hash to the previous entry's hash so that any modification or insertion between secured entries would break the chain. Because the hash function is deterministic, any minor change to the original data would completely change the resulting hash, allowing integrity verification.

question: How do I set up a new direct debit mandate for a customer so I can collect payments from them?
reference: In the Accounting app, go to Customers > Direct Debit Mandates and click New, then fill in the Customer, IBAN, SDD Scheme (CORE for B2C, B2B for B2B), and optionally an End Date. Click Send & Print to generate the mandate form PDF for the customer's signature, then click Validate to activate the mandate.

question: How do I restrict a shipping method so it only shows up for certain countries or when the order is under a certain weight?
reference: Use the Availability tab on the delivery method to define conditions based on the order's content or destination: set Countries to limit it to specific countries, and set Max Weight or Max Volume so the method is only available for orders below those limits. You can also use Must Have Tags and Excluded Tags to control availability based on product tags in the order.

question: How do I set up a tax so that part of the tax amount goes to a different account instead of the full amount being booked as tax payable?
reference: In the tax's Distribution for Invoices and Distribution for Refunds sections, add % of tax lines that split the tax amount (e.g. two 50% lines totaling 100%), and set the Account on each line to the account where that portion should be booked. Each line then creates a tax payable journal item using its own Account and Tax Grids, defaulting to the original invoice line's account if none is specified.

question: How do I scrap a product while I'm processing a receipt or delivery order in Odoo?
reference: In the Inventory app, click the # To Process button on the operation's task card, open the operation, then click the cog icon and select Scrap. In the Scrap Products pop-up, choose the product, adjust the quantity, specify a Lot/Serial number if tracked, and click Scrap Products; a Scraps smart button then appears on the operation form to view the scrap orders.

question: How do I move last year's profits into an equity account and then lock the books so nobody can change them?
reference: Create a new miscellaneous entry dated at the end of the fiscal year to book the current year's earnings to any equity account, then check that the current year's earnings line on the balance sheet shows a zero balance. Once confirmed, set the Hard Lock date to the last day of the fiscal year under Accounting > Accounting > Lock Dates, keeping in mind this date is irreversible.

question: How do I create an invoice by hand without going through a contract or a sales order?
reference: You can create invoices manually without using contracts or a sales order, which is recommended when you don't need to manage the sales process (quotations) or product/service delivery. Manual invoices are also useful for exceptional cases like creating a refund, giving a discount, modifying an invoice generated from a sales order, or invoicing something outside your core business.

question: How can I see extra columns like expiration date or last count date on the inventory adjustments screen that aren't showing up?
reference: Additional columns are hidden by default; to reveal them, click the column toggle and select the checkbox next to the column you want to display, such as Expiration Date or Last Count Date.

question: How can I make Odoo automatically check whether a customer's VAT number is valid for intra-community trade?
reference: Go to Accounting > Configuration > Settings, and in the Taxes section enable the Verify VAT Numbers feature, then click Save. Once enabled, Odoo checks the VAT number through VIES and automatically sets the Intra-Community Valid checkbox on contacts whose Tax ID is filled in and whose country differs from your company's.

question: How can I make Odoo pick the most recently received stock first when fulfilling orders?
reference: Set the product category's Force Removal Strategy to Last In, First Out (LIFO) and enable lot/serial tracking on the product. When you confirm a sales order, the delivery order will reserve the newest lot/serial numbers first; you can see which lots were picked in the Open: Stock move pop-up by clicking the bulleted list icon on the product line in the Operations tab.

question: How do I add a sub-variable to a report line in the accounting reports, and what do I need to fill in when creating it?
reference: Click Add a line within a report line to create an expression. You must give it a unique Label within that line and specify both a Computation Engine and a Formula; depending on the engine, subformulas may also be required.

question: How do I make sure my income account doesn't get messed up by the extra accounting entries when I use cash basis taxes?
reference: Set a Base Tax Received Account so your balance stays at zero and your income account isn't polluted by unnecessary movements. Go to Configuration > Settings > Taxes and select a Base Tax Received Account under Cash Basis.

question: How do I set up a new product so Odoo knows whether it's a physical item or a service I'm selling?
reference: In Odoo, both goods and services are set up as products. To create a new product, go to the Inventory app > Products > Products and click New, or select an existing product from the list to configure it; the fields you choose determine how the product is invoiced and tracked.

question: What counts as an expense versus income in Odoo's accounting setup?
reference: An expense is the cost of operations a company bears to generate revenues, such as supplier payments, employee wages, factory leases, and equipment depreciation. Income refers to the money, property, and other transfers of value received over a period in exchange for services or products.

question: How can I make sure my invoices meet the Basque Country's electronic invoicing rules, including sending them to the regional platforms and keeping records for audits?
reference: Odoo Invoicing supports Facturae XML for the FACe and e-Factura Euskadi platforms and integrates with TicketBAI for Basque compliance, letting you submit e-invoices to both national and regional systems. It also provides a secure, tamper-proof archive that keeps invoices for at least 6 years for audits, and automates VAT calculations and SII real-time reporting.

question: How can I find which of my lots or serial numbers are expired or about to expire?
reference: Go to Inventory > Products > Lots/Serial Numbers, clear any search filters, then click Filters and select Expiration Alerts. You can also open a specific Lot/Serial Number to see its Dates and a red Expiration Alert at the top if it's expired or expiring soon.

question: How do I set up a withholding tax in Odoo so I can apply it on customer invoices?
reference: Create a negative tax by going to Accounting > Configuration > Taxes and entering a negative amount in the Amount field, then in the Advanced Options tab create a retention Tax Group. If the retention is a percentage of a regular tax, create a Tax with the retention one in the Definition tab; once created, it can be used on customer forms, sales orders, and customer invoices.

question: How does Odoo handle electronic invoicing for Guatemalan tax requirements?
reference: Odoo's Invoicing and Accounting apps provide legally compliant e-invoicing for Guatemala's FEL system, issuing documents through a certified certifier and validating them with the SAT before delivery. Each authorized document is digitally signed, uses the SAT's XML/XSD format, and receives a certification date and unique UUID once validated.

question: How do I set up a shipping method so that a PDF label is generated automatically when I validate a delivery order?
reference: Go to Inventory > Configuration > Delivery > Shipping Methods, open the delivery method, and in the Configuration tab under Label Type choose one of the available label types. Once a sales order with that shipping company is confirmed and the delivery order is validated, the shipping label is automatically created as a PDF and appears in the Chatter.

question: How can I make Odoo reserve stock a few days ahead of the scheduled delivery date instead of right at it?
reference: Go to Inventory > Configuration > Operations Types, open the operation type, and in the General tab set the Reservation Method to Before scheduled date. A Reserve before scheduled date field then appears where you can set the number of days before (and days before when starred for favorited transfers) that products should be reserved.

question: How does Odoo help me stay compliant with Lithuanian e-invoicing rules, like keeping invoices for the required period and handling VAT?
reference: Odoo Invoicing supports Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 and XML formats, securely archives all invoices in a tamper-proof system for at least ten years as Lithuanian regulations require, and automates VAT calculations for both B2G and B2B transactions.

question: How do I put products into a package during a warehouse transfer like a receipt or delivery order?
reference: On the transfer, open the Operations tab and click the detailed operations icon on the product line, then in the pop-up click Add a line and assign the product to a Destination Package (select an existing one or type a new name and choose Create). Set the quantity in the Done column and click Confirm; alternatively, use the Put in Pack button to place everything in the transfer into a package.

question: How do I set up a budget for my profit and loss accounts so I can compare it against actual figures?
reference: Go to Accounting > Reporting > Profit and Loss, use the calendar button to choose a period, then click the Budget button and name the budget. A new column with the budget name appears next to the Balance column; assign amounts to each account you want to analyze, and a % column will show the current status.

question: How do I set up my products so that they get picked based on how close they are to expiring, and where do I configure the days for that?
reference: Enable the Lots and Serial Numbers and Expiration Dates features in Inventory app > Configuration > Settings, then on the product form's Inventory tab set Tracking to By Lots or By Unique Serial Number and select Expiration Date so the Removal Date field appears. The expiration date is the receipt date plus the days in the Expiration Date field, and the removal date is that expiration date minus the days in the Removal Date field.

question: How do I make sure my invoices comply with Italian e-invoicing rules when using Odoo?
reference: Odoo Invoicing supports Italy's legally compliant e-invoicing requirements: e-invoices must be submitted through the Sdi (Sistema di Interscambio) in the FatturaPA XML format, which is mandatory for B2B, B2C, and B2G transactions since 2019. Italy also supports Peppol standards for cross-border e-invoicing.

question: How do I control whether my warehouse staff can create new lot or serial numbers during a transfer, or only pick from ones that already exist?
reference: Enable Lots & Serial Numbers in Inventory > Configuration > Settings, then open the operation type and use the General tab: check 'Create New' to allow creating lots/serial numbers from that operation type, and check 'Use Existing ones' to allow selecting existing lot or serial numbers when creating transfers.

question: How can I let my customers pay their invoices instantly by scanning a barcode with their banking app?
reference: Enable EPC QR codes, which are two-dimensional barcodes customers scan with their mobile banking apps to initiate a SEPA credit transfer and pay invoices instantly. This feature is only available for companies in certain European countries such as Austria, Belgium, Finland, Germany, and the Netherlands.

question: How can I set up Odoo so my customers can create vendor bills on my behalf instead of me sending them invoices?
reference: Odoo supports self-billing, a workflow where the customer generates a vendor bill on the supplier's behalf and sends a copy for their records, removing the need for the supplier to issue a vendor bill. Odoo can generate self-billing vendor bills and self-billing credit notes, and these can be sent by email or via Peppol.

question: How can I set up a product so that Odoo only orders or produces it after a customer actually places an order, instead of keeping stock on hand?
reference: Use the Make to Order route: procurement or production is triggered only once a sales order is confirmed, and Odoo automatically links the sales order to the generated request for quotation or manufacturing order. This strategy suits customizable, high-value, low-demand products where holding inventory doesn't make sense.

question: How do I turn on multiple currencies in my accounting and set up automatic exchange rate updates?
reference: Go to Accounting > Configuration > Settings > Currencies and tick Multi-Currencies, then set a Journal, Gain Account, and Loss Account under 'Post Exchange difference entries in:' and click Save. To activate currencies, click Activate Other Currencies or go to Accounting > Configuration > Accounting: Currencies. For automatic rate updates, check Automatic Currency Rates, set the Interval and Service, and click Save; you can also click Update now (🗘) next to Next Run to refresh rates manually.

question: How do I give a customer their money back for a payment they made through Odoo?
reference: If your payment provider supports it, open the customer payment in Odoo and click the Refund button; no prior setup is needed. Some providers only allow full refunds, while others also support partial refunds.

question: How do I set up a Ponto account so my bank accounts sync with Odoo?
reference: Create an account on the Ponto website using the same email address as your Odoo profile, then log in, create an Organization with your contact details, and give consent for Ponto to access your bank data. Finally, click Accounts > Add account > Choose your bank, enter the bank account reference, and follow the on-screen steps to link each bank account you want synchronized with Odoo.

question: How can I sell a product in individual units if I buy it from my supplier in large packs?
reference: Odoo can be set up to use different units of measure for one product, so you can buy in a big pack and sell in individual units. This lets the system convert between the purchase unit and the sales unit.

question: How can I make sure my invoices meet Argentina's electronic invoicing rules when I bill customers there?
reference: Odoo Invoicing supports Argentina's authorized e-invoice formats, including FE with AFIP-compliant digital validation, XML with CAE authorization for real-time AFIP integration, and digitally signed PDF invoices with CAE and QR codes. It also provides tamper-proof archiving for the ten-year storage requirement and automatically calculates VAT and includes it on invoices to meet legal reporting requirements.

question: I want to set up DHL shipping in Odoo but I don't have a DHL Express account yet. What do I need to do to get the API credentials and where do I put them?
reference: First open a DHL Express account, then log in to the DHL developer portal, open the Apps tab from the user dashboard, and create an app following the four-step flow to obtain the API Key and API Secret. In Odoo, on the shipping method form, enter the DHL API Key in the DHL SiteID field and the API Secret in the DHL Password field.

question: How do I renumber a batch of vendor bills so they follow a continuous sequence after importing them from my old accounting system?
reference: Activate developer mode, select the bills in the vendor bills list view, open the Actions (gear) menu and choose Resequence, then pick the ordering (keep current order or reorder by accounting date), set the First New Sequence, and click Preview Modifications followed by Confirm. This feature requires administrator or advisor access, and resequencing fails with a Validation Error if entries are before a lock date, would create a duplicate, or the range is invalid.

question: How can I compare the numbers on a financial report between two different time periods?
reference: Click the Comparison menu on the report and select the periods you want to compare. You can also expand report lines with the right arrow and drill into details with the down arrow to annotate and view them.

question: Can I use AvaTax for my company based in Germany, and what are the main limitations I should know about?
reference: AvaTax integration is only available for databases/companies with locations in the United States, Canada, or Brazil, so a German-based company cannot use it. Also note that AvaTax uses the company address by default (enable Allow Ship Later in POS settings to use the warehouse address), and excise taxes such as tobacco/vape or fuel taxes are not supported.

question: Do I need to send electronic invoices when billing government agencies in Estonia, and what system do I use?
reference: Yes, since 2019 business-to-government (B2G) transactions in Estonia must use electronic invoices via the Rik's e-Invoicing System, the government's platform for public sector e-invoicing. Estonia is also part of the Peppol network for standardized cross-border e-invoicing.

question: How can I make sure no VAT gets charged when my company sells to another company within the same tax group?
reference: Create a fiscal position under Accounting > Configuration > Fiscal Positions, then in the Tax Mapping tab set the usual product tax as Tax on Product and the 0% tax as Tax to Apply (do the same in Account Mapping if needed). Then open the constituent company's contact card in the Contacts app, go to the Sales & Purchase tab, and set that fiscal position in the Fiscal Position field, repeating for each constituent company.

question: How can I make sure the oldest stock gets picked first when fulfilling orders, so older items don't sit around too long?
reference: Use the First In, First Out (FIFO) removal strategy, which selects products with the earliest arrival dates. For example, with lot-tracked T-shirts arriving August 1st and August 25th, an order on September 1st will pick the August 1st lots first.

question: How do I add shipping charges to a sales order so they show up on the customer's invoice?
reference: Open the sales order in the Sales app and click the Add Shipping button at the bottom-right, then choose the carrier in the Shipping Method field and click Get Rate to calculate the price before clicking Add. The delivery product then appears in the Order Lines tab with the shipping cost as its Unit Price, and after delivery you click Create invoice (then Create and View Invoice) to generate a draft invoice that includes the shipping cost in its Invoice Lines tab.

question: Where can I find and manage the lot numbers for my products in Odoo?
reference: Go to the Inventory app > Products > Lots/Serial Numbers to open the Lot/Serial Numbers dashboard. Lot numbers are grouped by product by default, and you can select a lot to modify its details or click New to create one.

question: How can I make Odoo pick products with the closest expiration date first when fulfilling orders?
reference: Use the FEFO (First Expiry, First Out) removal strategy, which prioritizes picking goods with the nearest expiration date to minimize spoilage. Removal strategies are configured for warehouses and determine which products are taken and in what order.

question: How does Odoo handle electronic invoicing requirements for Romania, and is it compliant with the local e-invoicing system?
reference: Odoo Invoicing supports Romania's regulatory standards, including the RO e-Factura national platform for issuing and receiving standardized electronic invoices, which is mandatory for B2G transactions and certain high-risk B2B sectors. Romania is also integrated with the Peppol network for cross-border e-invoicing and EU compliance.

question: Do I need to send electronic invoices to government clients in the Netherlands, and how does Odoo help with that?
reference: Yes, B2G transactions in the Netherlands must comply with the European Standard EN 16931 under EU Directive 2014/55/EU, and public sector entities accept e-invoices through platforms such as Digipoort. Odoo Invoicing supports legally compliant e-invoicing for the Netherlands, including the Peppol network for standardized cross-border transactions.

question: How do I make Odoo reserve whatever stock is available for an order instead of only reserving complete packages?
reference: Go to Inventory app > Configuration > Product Categories, open the desired category, and in the Logistics section set Reserve Packagings to Reserve Partial Packagings. The Product Packaging feature must be enabled first under Inventory app > Configuration > Settings in the Products section.

question: How can I see the value of each lot or serial number in my inventory?
reference: Go to Inventory app > Reporting > Valuation, click the search bar, and under the Group By section select Lot/Serial number. Then click the plus icon next to a collapsed lot number line to expand it.

question: How do I create a purchase order in Odoo and confirm it?
reference: Go to the Purchase app and click New to open a blank Request for Quotation form, add a vendor in the Vendor field, fill out the other fields as needed, and add products under the Products tab with Add a product. When ready, click Confirm Order to move it to the Purchase Order stage; a Receipt smart button then appears at the top of the form.

question: How can I automatically change the taxes and accounts applied to transactions for certain customers or vendors?
reference: Use fiscal positions, which let you create rules that automatically adapt the taxes and accounts used for a transaction. They can be applied automatically, manually, or assigned to a partner, and several default fiscal positions come with your fiscal localization package.

question: How can I make my payments create journal entries instead of just sitting there without accounting entries?
reference: You can configure your bank and cash journals to use outstanding accounts. Incoming payments post to an outstanding receipts account and outgoing payments post to an outstanding payments account until they are reconciled with bank transactions; these accounts are usually Current Assets and Current Liabilities.

question: How does Odoo help me stay compliant with Austrian e-invoicing rules, like the required invoice formats and how long invoices are kept?
reference: Odoo supports standard e-invoice formats such as PDF with digital signatures and XML in UBL format, compatible with Austria's e-rechnung.gv.at platform, and it securely archives all invoices in a tamper-proof system for the required minimum of seven years. It also automatically calculates and includes VAT in invoices, ensuring each invoice follows the legal format for B2B and B2G transactions.

question: How do I set up a rule so that a specific product gets automatically stored in a particular sub-location when it arrives in my warehouse?
reference: First enable the Multi-Step Routes feature under Inventory app > Configuration > Settings (which also activates Storage Locations), then go to Inventory app > Configuration > Putaway Rules and click New. Set the Product or Product Category, the When product arrives in location, and the Store to location (which must be a sub-location of the arrival location), then click Save.
